chapter_theme: The vision of Siva (சிவ தரிசனம்): Siva is not other than the mind, and appears within the mind made clear; he is the subtle hidden thing in which speech and mind vanish, without going, coming or ruin; beyond the Supreme and all dispute, he gives grace in the world as Hara.

2853.reading: There is no difference between what is called the mind and what is called Siva; Siva appears within the mind; for those who can clear the mind more and more, Siva abides within the mind.
2853.nuance: Every line begins with சிந்தை (mind, thought). The first line states identity, the rest presence: Siva appears in, and dwells in, the mind as it is cleared. Read together, the identity may hold only of the cleared mind; the verse leaves both readings open.

2854.reading: Look at the hidden thing in which speech and mind disappear: the thing to be seen is subtle; for those who examine and grasp it there is no going, no coming and no ruin, and even its gain is the Father.
2854.nuance: போக்கு, வரவு, கேடு (going, coming, ruin) can describe the hidden thing itself or the knower, for whom birth and death end. The last line, யாக்கமும் அத்தனை, is obscure: it may be 'ஆக்கமும் அத்தனை' (even its growth is that much) or point to அத்தன், the Father.

2855.reading: Being the Supreme, becoming the Supreme beyond the supreme and going further, being strength and the bright flame itself beyond all dispute, being the bearer whom no one can know as their own, he gave grace in the world as Hara.
2855.nuance: பரன், பராபரன், உரன், தரன் and அரன் rhyme through the verse, rising to the transcendent and returning as Hara, who gives grace in the world. வழக்கற (beyond dispute, or beyond usage and speech) and தனதென ஆறு அறிவொண்ணா are compressed.

links.note: If 2854's 'no going, no coming' is read of the knower, both say that examining and grasping what truly is ends birth: the Kural's mind that ponders and knows what is need not think of birth again.
2804 places the Lord as Om, fire and right order within the heart; 2853 goes further and says the mind and Siva are not different, Siva showing within the mind as it clears.

2853 says there is no difference between what is called the mind and Siva (சிந்தையது என்னச் சிவனென்ன வேறில்லை); 2017 uses the same formula for the soul (சீவன் எனச் சிவன் என்ன வேறில்லை) and adds that souls do not know it until they do. Both deny a gap and make knowing the condition: 2853 by clearing the mind (சிந்தை தெளிய), 2017 by the soul knowing Siva.

1896 says that when speech and mind are both still it is silence, and the pure are those in whom they are; 2854 points to the hidden thing in which speech and mind disappear (வாக்கும் மனமும் மறைந்த மறைபொருள்) and says the one who grasps it has no going, coming or ruin. 1896 describes the practice of stilling வாக்கு and மனம்; 2854 names what is found where they vanish.

2855 says he is the Supreme, the Paraparan, strength, the bright flame, the bearer, and as Hara gave grace (பரனாய் ... உரனாய் ... ஒண்சுடர் தானாய் தரனாய் ... அரனாய்); 2861 takes the same list and denies each item (பரன்அல்ல ... உரன்அல்ல ... ஒண்சுடர் அல்ல தரன்அல்ல ... அரன்அல்ல), placing it beyond bliss. 2861 itself joins the two (தான் அவையாய் அல்லவாகும்): being all these it is none of them, so it limits 2855's names rather than cancelling them.

source_issues: 2854: line 4 begins யாக்கமும், which may stand for ஆக்கமும் with a glide consonant or be a misprint; the sense is unclear.
